label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 2 · Question 7
knowledgePattern: Translate gradient and intercept signs into necessary versus sufficient coefficient conditions
solution:
Rearranging gives y=−(a/b)x+c/b. Both gradient and intercept are positive exactly when a has the opposite sign from b, while c has the same sign as b. Hence a and c must have opposite signs.

That last condition alone is not sufficient: a=−1,c=1,b=−1 has opposite signs for a,c but gives gradient−1 and intercept−1. Thus E is necessary but not sufficient.

A includes the full two-sign conditions and is sufficient as well. C is not necessary (take a=−1,b=c=1), and D is not necessary (take a=1,b=c=−1). B is incompatible with a positive gradient and intercept. Answer E.

hints.title: Read the two features from the equation
hints.body: Rearrange the equation into y=mx+d. Express the sign conditions on m and d in terms of the coefficients.
hints.recap: In slope-intercept form, the coefficient of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> gives the gradient and the constant gives the vertical intercept.
hints.pitfall: Do not assume any coefficient is positive merely because it is nonzero.
hints.pause: List the possible coefficient sign patterns.

hints.title: Separate the two directions
hints.body: A necessary condition must hold in every allowed sign pattern. To show it is not sufficient, find coefficients obeying that condition but failing a required line feature.
hints.recap: Necessary means forced by the result; sufficient means strong enough to guarantee it.
hints.pitfall: Changing an unmentioned coefficient can matter.
hints.pause: Test the proposed conditions and supply a counterexample for the insufficient direction.
